# Configuration

Server configuration is entirely CLI flags; run `seavxrouter -h` for the full
list. No `.env` file is loaded automatically.

## Credentials file

`seavxrouter login` manages `~/.seavx/auth.jsonc`. JSON with `//` comments
allowed, mode `0600`. Never commit it or paste its contents into an issue.

```jsonc
// ~/.seavx/auth.jsonc — generated by `seavxrouter login`; keep private.
[
  {
    "provider": "antigravity",
    "access_token": "REDACTED",
    "refresh_token": "REDACTED",
    "expiry": "2026-11-14T10:03:42+07:00",
    "project_id": "REDACTED",
    "tier": "g1-pro-tier",
    "email": "you@example.com"
  },
  {
    "provider": "groq",
    "access_token": "gsk_REDACTED",
    "refresh_token": "",
    "expiry": "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  },
  {
    "provider": "cloudflare",
    "access_token": "REDACTED",
    "refresh_token": "",
    "expiry": "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "account_id": "REDACTED"
  }
]
```

Multiple entries for the same provider become accounts in that provider's
rotation pool. The running server watches this file; adding a provider or
account through `seavxrouter login` takes effect without a restart. Entries whose
credentials are unchanged keep their in-memory identity so per-account quota
state survives the reload.

## Environment variables

Optional variables that save typing during `seavxrouter login`; the OpenCode
ones also control how the running router reaches its local server:

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `NVIDIA_API_KEY` | Key read by `seavxrouter login nvidia` instead of prompting. |
| `GROQ_API_KEY` | Key read by `seavxrouter login groq` instead of prompting. |
| `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` | Token read by `seavxrouter login cloudflare`. |
| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` | Account ID used by Cloudflare requests and login. |
| `OPENCODE_SERVER_URL` | Use an existing OpenCode v2 server instead of auto-starting one. |
| `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` | Basic-auth username for that server (default `opencode`). |
| `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` | Basic-auth password for that server. |
| `OPENCODE_BIN` | OpenCode binary to auto-start (default `opencode` on `PATH`). |

## Local state

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `~/.seavx/auth.jsonc` | Provider credentials, mode `0600`. |
| `~/.seavx/usage.db` | SQLite usage ledger and recent request logs. |
| `~/.seavx/hidden-models.txt` | Optional model blocklist. |
| `~/.seavx/cache/models.json` | Cached models.dev pricing catalog. |
| `~/.seavx/server.url` | URL of the running server, used by the TUI. |

Set `-auth-file` to move `auth.jsonc`; `hidden-models.txt` always sits next to
it.

## Hidden models

`hidden-models.txt` removes model IDs from discovery and makes them
unrequestable (`404 model_not_found`). One entry per line:

```text
# literal IDs and provider-wide prefixes
nvidia/broken-model
codebuddy/
```

Blank lines and `#` comments are ignored. The file is re-read when its mtime
changes; no restart is needed.

## Usage and pricing

Every completed `/v1/*` request can be recorded in SQLite with token counts and
an estimated USD cost. Prices come from the models.dev catalog (cached locally)
with a built-in fallback. Override or extend with a JSON file:

```json
{
  "my-model": {"input": 0.5, "output": 1.5, "cached": 0.1}
}
```

```bash
./seavxrouter -pricing ./prices.json
```

Prices are USD per one million tokens. Disable tracking with `-usage-db off`.

## Request logs and compression

The newest 1,000 requests are retained with response bodies (up to 10 MB each),
status, latency, provider, model, user, and token usage. Request bodies are read
for routing hints but never persisted. Read them through `/v1/logging` or the
TUI; live entries arrive over `/v1/logging/stream`.

Large tool results in incoming requests are compressed before forwarding to
reduce prompt tokens. Tune with `-compress` and `-compress-min-bytes`; inspect
cumulative savings at `/v1/compression`.

## Quotas

Providers that expose quota report it at `/v1/quota`, aggregated per account.
Quota errors rotate accounts and may fail over to another provider, as described
in `references/providers.md`.

## Security

- The server binds to `127.0.0.1` by default and has no authentication until
  `-api-key` is set. Never expose an unauthenticated instance to a network.
- Credentials are stored in plaintext (`0600`) so tokens can be refreshed.
  Protect the host and the file.
- `usage.db` contains response bodies and can contain sensitive data.
- For remote access, terminate TLS at a reverse proxy and require the API key.
- If a credential leaks, revoke it with the provider and log in again. Report
  vulnerabilities per `SECURITY.md`.
